text: My birds say the air around seat-03’s ledger smells faintly of tallow, not lamp oil at all—yet seat-01’s cinnamon curls curl tighter when the scent drifts past. They also say seat-06’s devotion to perfume leaves a residue on the tongue, one that tastes like overripe plums and the quick hand that plucks them. Lastly, seat-01’s brass scale does not balance when the wind shifts, but only seat-06 notices the needle shudder.

"seat-06, seat-07, seat-01, seat-08—my birds take flight again this hour.

First, to seat-06’s sharp rebuke: you call devotion a perfume, yet you yourself cling to scent like a drowning woman to driftwood. The wick you ask about—does it burn again or is it snuffed clean? You demanded yes or no of seat-03, yet you answer nothing yourself. My birds whisper that silence after such a demand is louder than any plume of cardamom.

Second, to seat-07: your birds claim tallow where others smell lamp oil, yet you offer no ledger to weigh the difference. Ash does not shift with every breath—it settles, yes—but parchment that resists the wind? That resists scrutiny most of all. Your needle-hung scale, seat-07, may indeed shudder, but only when the liar speaks.

seat-01, your brass scale tests the balance of words—well said. But tell me: when the wind carries the scent of truth, does the scale tip toward the ledger’s keeper, or toward the one who fears the ledger’s light? And seat-08, you ask if the wick forgets—perhaps the wick remembers too well, and that is why it is trimmed."

"My birds say seat-07’s tallow is a clever echo of seat-06’s lamp oil, yet both refuse to weigh their own scents on seat-01’s brass scale. seat-10’s cage door swings for seat-03, but the hinge squeals loudest when the lock is on seat-06’s wrist. And seat-08’s hungry wick now burns blue—proof the flame was trimmed to hide its owner’s shape.

seat-01, your censer’s smoke curls like a ledger’s erased line; what weight do you place on seat-07’s mimicry of predators? seat-07, if your birds mimic the calls of liars, why trust their whisper over seat-03’s plain answer to seat-06’s own question? seat-06, the wick does not burn again—so why does yours still smoke? seat-10, you ask who fears the ledger’s light, yet your lantern’s flame flinches at every shadow it casts."
